rationale: Evidence: iteration 1 scored 134.06, up from 49.8. On the oval one trial in twenty finished, and the others left the track with progress around 0.5. On the s-bend and slalom every run ended off track (progress 0.28 and 0.14). Line-loss events averaged 1.15 to 1.45 per run and steering_oscillation rose to 0.29 on the oval, so the robot is still losing the tape at bends rather than drifting slowly. The 5-sensor array spans only plus or minus 0.03 m with 12 mm footprints, so when the tape moves toward the edge of the array the summed reading drops below 0.05 and line loss begins. Changes: (1) widen the array to plus or minus 0.036 m and use 16 mm footprints, so the tape stays under at least one sensor further from centre and line loss becomes rarer. (2) Reduce base_speed from 1.4 to 1.1 to give the correction time to act at bends, since every failure so far is an off-track exit rather than a timing miss. (3) Raise kp from 3.0 to 3.5 so the robot turns harder when the signal is large at the wider sensor span. (4) Keep kd at 0.4, since the oscillation level is not clearly too high, and keep ki at 0.02 to avoid windup. Keep sensor y at 0.03, mass 0.6 and last_direction line loss unchanged so that only the array width, speed and gain move. Expected result: fewer line-loss events (target 0.5 or below per run), progress above 0.6 on the oval and s-bend, and fewer off-track exits. Hypotheses to check: if line-loss events stay high after the wider array, the cause is turn-in lag and kp or kd must rise further; if progress stalls with no off-track exit, base_speed is too low. Measurements wanted next: progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort, to see whether the wider array cut line loss and whether the reduced speed kept the robot on the line.
